Net revenue retention (NRR) answers one question: if you stopped selling today, would revenue grow or shrink? See ::postlink[net-revenue-retention-guide] for the long version.

## The formula

NRR = (starting MRR + expansion - contraction - churn) / starting MRR

If you start the month at $100,000, add $8,000 in upgrades, lose $3,000 to downgrades and $4,000 to churn, NRR is $101,000 / $100,000 = 101%.

## Benchmarks

| Segment | Median NRR | Top quartile |
|---|---|---|
| SMB | 97% | 105% |
| Mid-market | 104% | 115% |
| Enterprise | 110% | 125% |

## Why involuntary churn matters here

Every failed payment you do not recover counts as churn in that formula. Recovering a $500 account is worth the same to NRR as winning a $500 upsell.

*Payment recovery is the cheapest NRR lever most teams have.* It needs no sales call and no new feature, just ::postlink[stripe-failed-payment-recovery].

### A note on cohorts

Read NRR by cohort, not as one number: a 2024 cohort at 120% can hide a 2025 cohort at 90%.
